difficultyAxis: Sheer breadth under one budget: eight interrelated entities, ten user stories and twenty-six acceptance scenarios, so an implementation must sustain consistency across the whole specification rather than the first half of it.
rationale: A clinic service that combines entity count, attribute width and story count in a single task. Stories share entities (an appointment references a patient, a practitioner and a room; an encounter references an appointment; a prescription references an encounter and carries items; a diagnosis references an encounter). A generator that truncates its work, drops the tail entities or the last stories, or loses cross-story consistency is visibly wrong here while the smaller fixtures still pass.

userStories.intent: register a patient with a medical record number and demographic details
userStories.benefit: the patient can be booked and treated under one identity

scenarios.given: a medical record number matching the permitted pattern and a date of birth in the past
scenarios.when: the clerk registers the patient
scenarios.then: the patient is persisted and returned with its generated identifier

scenarios.given: a malformed email address
scenarios.when: the clerk attempts to register the patient
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid before reaching the service layer

scenarios.given: a date of birth in the future
scenarios.when: the clerk attempts to register the patient
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid

userStories.intent: register a practitioner with a speciality and a consultation fee
userStories.benefit: appointments can be assigned to a qualified clinician

scenarios.given: a registration number matching the permitted pattern and a non-negative fee
scenarios.when: the manager registers the practitioner
scenarios.then: the practitioner is persisted and returned with its identifier

scenarios.given: a negative consultation fee
scenarios.when: the manager attempts to register the practitioner
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid

userStories.intent: register a room with a floor, a capacity and its surgical equipment flag
userStories.benefit: appointments can be placed in a suitable room

scenarios.given: a unique room code and a capacity within the permitted range
scenarios.when: the manager registers the room
scenarios.then: the room is persisted and returned with its identifier

scenarios.given: a capacity below the permitted minimum
scenarios.when: the manager attempts to register the room
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid

userStories.intent: book an appointment for a patient with a practitioner in a room
userStories.benefit: the patient has a confirmed slot with a clinician

scenarios.given: an existing patient, an existing active practitioner, an existing room and a start time before the end time
scenarios.when: the clerk books the appointment
scenarios.then: the appointment is persisted with all three references and returned with its identifier

scenarios.given: a practitioner who already holds an overlapping appointment
scenarios.when: the clerk attempts to book the appointment
scenarios.then: the service rejects the booking as conflicting

scenarios.given: an end time earlier than the start time
scenarios.when: the clerk attempts to book the appointment
scenarios.then: the service rejects the appointment as inconsistent

scenarios.given: a patient identifier that does not exist
scenarios.when: the clerk attempts to book the appointment
scenarios.then: the service reports the patient as not found

userStories.intent: record the encounter that took place for a patient
userStories.benefit: the clinical record reflects what happened during the visit

scenarios.given: an existing patient, an existing practitioner and a start time not in the future
scenarios.when: the clinician records the encounter
scenarios.then: the encounter is persisted and returned with its identifier

scenarios.given: an end time earlier than the start time
scenarios.when: the clinician attempts to record the encounter
scenarios.then: the service rejects the encounter as inconsistent

scenarios.given: an appointment identifier that does not exist
scenarios.when: the clinician records the encounter against that appointment
scenarios.then: the service reports the appointment as not found

userStories.intent: record one or more diagnoses against an encounter, marking one as primary
userStories.benefit: the reason for treatment is coded and unambiguous

scenarios.given: an existing encounter and a diagnosis code matching the permitted pattern
scenarios.when: the clinician records the diagnosis
scenarios.then: the diagnosis is persisted against the encounter and returned with its identifier

scenarios.given: an encounter that already carries a primary diagnosis
scenarios.when: the clinician records a second diagnosis marked primary
scenarios.then: the service rejects the second primary diagnosis as conflicting

scenarios.given: an encounter identifier that does not exist
scenarios.when: the clinician records a diagnosis against it
scenarios.then: the service reports the encounter as not found

userStories.intent: issue a prescription for an encounter with a validity date
userStories.benefit: the patient can obtain the medication after the visit

scenarios.given: an existing encounter and a validity date in the future
scenarios.when: the clinician issues the prescription
scenarios.then: the prescription is persisted against the encounter and returned with its identifier

scenarios.given: a validity date in the past
scenarios.when: the clinician attempts to issue the prescription
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid

userStories.intent: add medication items to an existing prescription
userStories.benefit: the dispensed medication and dosage are explicit

scenarios.given: an existing prescription and a quantity within the permitted range
scenarios.when: the clinician adds the item
scenarios.then: the item is persisted against the prescription

scenarios.given: a quantity above the permitted maximum
scenarios.when: the clinician attempts to add the item
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid

scenarios.given: a prescription identifier that does not exist
scenarios.when: the clinician attempts to add an item to it
scenarios.then: the service reports the prescription as not found

userStories.intent: reschedule an existing appointment to a new slot
userStories.benefit: a cancellation can be absorbed without losing the booking

scenarios.given: an existing booked appointment and a free future slot
scenarios.when: the clerk reschedules the appointment
scenarios.then: the appointment stores the new start and end times and remains booked

scenarios.given: an appointment that has already been attended
scenarios.when: the clerk attempts to reschedule it
scenarios.then: the service rejects the reschedule as conflicting with the current state

userStories.intent: read the appointments booked for an existing patient
userStories.benefit: the patient's schedule can be reviewed

scenarios.given: a patient with no appointments
scenarios.when: the manager reads the patient's appointments
scenarios.then: the service returns an empty collection rather than reporting an error

scenarios.given: a patient identifier that does not exist
scenarios.when: the manager reads the patient's appointments
scenarios.then: the service reports the patient as not found
